//! bare-env: start a program with exactly the environment given on the command line (NAME=value arguments before
//! `--`) and nothing inherited, the way Rust's `Command::env_clear()` does; stdin, stdout and stderr are passed
//! through, and the program's exit code is this program's. Node cannot do this on Windows (it fills a few system
//! names in from its own environment), so this is how the captures see what the real codex does with none of them.
//!
//!   bare-env [NAME=value ...] -- program [args ...]
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
fn main() {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    let split = args.iter().position(|a| a == "--").expect("usage: bare-env [NAME=value ...] -- program [args]");
    let mut cmd = Command::new(&args[split + 1]);
    cmd.args(&args[split + 2..]).env_clear().stdin(Stdio::inherit()).stdout(Stdio::inherit()).stderr(Stdio::inherit());
    for pair in &args[..split] {
        let (k, v) = pair.split_once('=').expect("NAME=value");
        cmd.env(k, v);
    }
    match cmd.status() {
        Ok(status) => std::process::exit(status.code().unwrap_or(1)),
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("bare-env: could not start: {e}");
            std::process::exit(127);
        }
    }
}
